# telnyx_network_route (Data Source)

A route on a network that sends traffic for a CIDR through a next hop.



<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `id` (String) Identifies the resource.

### Read-Only

- `cidr` (String) The IPv4 CIDR the route covers.
- `created_at` (String) ISO 8601 formatted date-time indicating when the resource was created.
- `network_id` (String) The id of the Network the route belongs to.
- `next_hop` (Attributes) Where the Network sends traffic for the route's CIDR. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--next_hop))
- `origin` (String) `static` for a route added with `POST /network_routes`, `attachment` for a route that another resource installed and removes.
- `record_type` (String) Identifies the type of the resource.
- `status` (String) `pending` until Telnyx installs the route on the Network, then `active`. `inactive` while a tunnel next hop has no connected process. `failed` (Preview, not reported yet) when Telnyx could not install the route.

<a id="nestedatt--next_hop"></a>
### Nested Schema for `next_hop`

Read-Only:

- `id` (String) The id of the tunnel or attachment.
- `type` (String) The type of the next hop. Routes added with `POST /network_routes` use `tunnel`. Routes that attachments install carry the attachment's type. One of `tunnel`, `wireguard_peer`.
